event: Elsie wakes to the bread smell in the dark and dresses fast, to see the Marigold off.
She takes the slice of honey cake the baker brought last night, saved and wrapped in paper.
At the Long Cut the Marigold has her fire lit, and Nell is coiling ropes on the roof.
Tamsin comes off the plank with red eyes and a bundle of letters tied up under her arm.
She says she wrote half the night: an answer to every one of Nell's.
Elsie gives Rosa the saved slice of honey cake, and Rosa eats it on the spot.
Rosa says that's the next cake paid for in advance, and kisses Elsie on both cheeks.
Nell hugs Elsie and whispers to her to keep Tamsin safe.
Elsie whispers back that she will, and that Tamsin keeps her safe too.

changes.note: Bond: Nell 2 → 3 (kindness: a hug and a whispered promise at the plank)

event: Tamsin hands Nell the bundle of letters; Nell holds it to her chest and can't speak.
Rosa tells Tamsin her bunk stays made up, and the Marigold is back next month.
The lock's black gates swing open, and the Marigold goes through with Nell waving her kerchief.
Tamsin stands at the lock's edge until the barge is gone round the bend.
Elsie takes her hand, and down the Tether the ache in Tamsin is a good one now.

changes.note: Bond: Tamsin 37 → 38 (kindness: Elsie takes her hand at the lock)

event: Tamsin says she'll be at the wharf for the Marigold's next tie-up, and every one after.
They walk back along the canals as the mist lifts off the Mere.
On Willow Canal a narrow house has a card in its window: to let.
Elsie stops dead: a blue door, window boxes, and a wild garden spilling over the wall.
She presses her nose to the glass: a kitchen big enough for a long table and six chairs.
Tamsin reads the card: apply to the letting agent on Coin Street.
Elsie says it's what she meant at the Poppy: all of them under one roof.
Tamsin looks at the house, then at her, and says they could never pay for it.
Elsie says not yet, and writes the street in her notebook.
At the guild hall Tilly waits by the board with soot on her nose.
Elsie tells her about the blue-doored house all in one breath, and Tilly lights up.
Tilly asks if there'd be room for a still; Elsie says there's a whole shed in the garden.
Cora comes out of the charcoal door with a dried lavender sprig still in her buttonhole.
Elsie sees the lavender and beams, and Cora looks very hard at the board.
The glowcaps notice is still up on the F-rank board: glowcaps from the Underbloom for a dyer.
Tilly goes white at the word Underbloom, then says she went down for the goat and can again.
Elsie asks if she's sure; Tilly says yes, if Elsie holds her hand on the stair.
The clerk enters the party for the glowcaps, and Cora writes it in her ledger.
At the old flower market the clerk at the stair head logs them in, and Tamsin pays the licence.

changes.note: Tamsin pays the Underbloom licence at the stair head: 1 lantern, 111 → 101

event: Elsie takes Tilly's hand at the top of the stair, and Tilly's fingers are ice cold.
Elsie hums all the way down, and Tilly counts the steps out loud.
The first floor's brick cellars glow with pale flowers, and Tilly breathes out at last.
The notice says glowcaps grow in damp corners, so they follow the drip-lines on the walls.
A bloom beetle the size of a cat grazes by a wall, and Elsie wishes it good morning.
In a dripping alcove they find glowcaps: pale blue mushrooms, glowing softly.
Tilly lets go of Elsie's hand to pick them, chattering about dye.
Elsie picks beside her, and Tilly's shoulder stays pressed to hers the whole time.
Tamsin follows the drips down a side passage to look for more.
Stranglevine whips round Tamsin's legs and arms and hauls her off her feet.
Tamsin roars and strains, and the vine pulls tighter.
Elsie feels it at once down the Tether, a crushing round her own ribs.
Elsie runs to her; Cora catches her arm and says the vine takes whoever brushes it.
Tilly fumbles a flame vial, her hands shaking too hard to pull the stopper.
Elsie takes Tilly's hands in hers a moment, and says she knows Tilly can.
Tilly's hands go steady; she lights the vial and lays fire along the vine's root.
The vine shrieks and lets go, and Tamsin drops into Elsie's arms.
Tamsin laughs on the floor and says that's twice now Elsie has caught her.
Elsie checks her over for bruises, ribs first, and Tamsin goes quiet under her hands.
Cora writes in her ledger; Elsie asks if it's skills used, and Cora says it's Tilly.
Tilly stares at her own steady hands as if they belong to somebody else.
They fill the dyer's sack with glowcaps, and Tilly carries it like treasure.
They climb the stair into daylight, and the clerk logs them out.
On Vat Street the dyer has blue hands to the elbow, and boils glowcaps into a glowing blue.
She pays on the spot; Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly share it, and Elsie gives Tilly the odd pips.
The dyer shows Elsie a bolt of the glowing blue cloth, and Elsie gasps.
At the Tipsy Heron Elsie pays for four bowls of stew, Cora's too, and Cora lets her.
Elsie asks them all at once about the blue-doored house on Willow Canal.
Tamsin says it'd cost more than all their purses; Tilly says she'd sleep in the shed.
Elsie asks Cora if a Warden could live with her party; Cora says the Accord says nothing of it.
Elsie asks if that means no; Cora says, after a long while, that it means it's allowed.
Cora writes in her ledger, and Tilly cranes to see, and Cora shuts it.
Cora says she has her report to write, and goes back across the canal to the hall.
Elsie, Tamsin and Tilly go to Coin Street and ask the letting agent about the house.
The agent says two suns a month and a month in hand, and eyes Tamsin's axe.
Tilly does sums on her fingers and says that's a great many glowcaps.
Elsie asks him to keep it for them; he laughs, and says whoever comes with the coin first has it.
Outside, Tamsin says they'll take bigger quests, and Elsie says yes, and Tilly says yes.
They pile all three hands together in the street and shake on it.
Tamsin goes back to the hall to read the E-rank notices.
Tilly walks Elsie home and asks if she'd really give Tilly the shed.
Elsie says the shed and the room beside hers, and Tilly trips on the kerb.
At the Honeycomb door Tilly hugs her hard and runs off talking to herself.
In the attic Elsie draws the blue-doored house in her notebook, with a room for each of them.
She draws a room for Cora too, and looks at it a long time.
She tells Sunny the lemon they might be moving, and that there's a garden.
Down the Tether Tamsin is busy and loud, and then all at once fond.
The lamplighters' boats go by below the round window, lighting the canal lantern by lantern.
She writes her mother: I think I've found the place where I'll stay.
A tap comes at the attic door, and it's Tamsin with a fistful of E-rank notices.
They read them lying side by side on Elsie's narrow bed.
Tamsin falls asleep halfway through a notice about river trolls, her head on Elsie's pillow.
Elsie pulls the quilt over her and lies down beside her on what's left of the bed.
Asleep, Tamsin finds Elsie's hand and holds on to it.
